options.B: A and C are independent.
options.C: B and C are independent.
options.D:

questions.explaination: Sample space $S = \{HH, HT, TH, TT\}$. Events are $A = \{HH\}$, $B = \{HH, HT\}$, $C = \{HH, TH\}$. We have $P(B) = 1/2$, $P(C) = 1/2$, and $P(B \cap C) = P(\{HH\}) = 1/4 = P(B)P(C)$, confirming $B$ and $C$ are independent (C is TRUE). The chromatic number of a graph is the minimum number of colours used in a
proper colouring of the graph. Let 𝐺 be any graph with 𝑛 vertices and chromatic
number 𝑘. Which of the following statements is/are always TRUE?

questions.explaination: A proper $k$-coloring partitions the $n$ vertices into $k$ independent sets. By the Pigeonhole Principle, at least one of these independent sets has size $\ge \lceil n/k \rceil \ge n/k$ (B is TRUE). In addition, every pair of color classes must have at least one edge between them (otherwise those two colors could be merged, yielding a $(k-1)$-coloring), requiring at least $\binom{k}{2} = \frac{k(k-1)}{2}$ edges (C is TRUE).

Addresses `0xA248` (P) and `0xA262` (S) both evaluate to block offset within block `0xA240`, which maps to line 9. Let 𝐺 be a directed graph and 𝑇 a depth first search (DFS) spanning tree in 𝐺 that
is rooted at a vertex 𝑣. Suppose 𝑇 is also a breadth first search (BFS) tree in 𝐺,
rooted at 𝑣. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE for every such graph 𝐺
and tree 𝑇 ?

options.A: There are no back-edges in 𝐺 with respect to the tree 𝑇
options.B: There are no cross-edges in 𝐺 with respect to the tree 𝑇

questions.subtopic: Graph traversals, minimum spanning trees, shortest paths
questions.explaination: In a BFS tree $T$, any edge $(u, w)$ in $G$ must connect vertices whose BFS levels differ by at most 1 (i.e., $\text{level}(w) \le \text{level}(u) + 1$). A forward-edge in a DFS tree goes from ancestor $u$ to descendant $w$ with $\text{level}(w) \ge \text{level}(u) + 2$. If such an edge existed in $G$, BFS would explore $w$ directly from $u$ at depth $\text{level}(u) + 1$, contradicting the structure of $T$. Hence, no forward-edges can exist in $G$ with respect to $T$ (C is TRUE).

Suppose you are asked to design a new reliable byte-stream transport protocol
like TCP. This protocol, named myTCP, runs over a 100 Mbps network with Round
Trip Time of 150 milliseconds and the maximum segment lifetime of 2 minutes.
Which of the following is/are valid lengths of the Sequence Number ﬁeld in the
myTCP header?

options.A: 30 bits
options.B: 32 bits
options.C: 34 bits
options.D:
36 bits
CS

questions.subtopic: Transport layer: flow control and congestion control, UDP, TCP, sockets
questions.explaination: To prevent sequence number wraparound within the Maximum Segment Lifetime ($MSL = 2\text{ min} = 120\text{ s}$), the sequence number space $2^k$ must be at least the data bytes transmitted at line rate during MSL: $2^k \ge \frac{100 \times 10^6\text{ bps}}{8} \times 120\text{ s} = 1.5 \times 10^9\text{ bytes}$. Since $2^{30} \approx 1.07 \times 10^9 < 1.5 \times 10^9$ and $2^{31} \approx 2.15 \times 10^9 > 1.5 \times 10^9$, at least 31 bits are required. Thus, 32 bits, 34 bits, and 36 bits are all valid lengths.

Suppose in a web browser, you click on the www.gate-2023.in URL. The browser
cache is empty. The IP address for this URL is not cached in your local host, so
a DNS lookup is triggered (by the local DNS server deployed on your local host)
over the 3-tier DNS hierarchy in an iterative mode. No resource records are cached
anywhere across all DNS servers.
Let RTT denote the round trip time between your local host and DNS servers
in the DNS hierarchy. The round trip time between the local host and the web
server hosting www.gate-2023.in is also equal to RTT. The HTML ﬁle associated
with the URL is small enough to have negligible transmission time and negligible
rendering time by your web browser, which references 10 equally small objects on
the same web server.
Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT about the minimum elapsed
time between clicking on the URL and your browser fully rendering it?

options.A: 7 RTTs, in case of non-persistent HTTP with 5 parallel TCP connections.
options.B: 5 RTTs, in case of persistent HTTP with pipelining.
options.C: 9 RTTs, in case of non-persistent HTTP with 5 parallel TCP connections.
options.D:
6 RTTs, in case of persistent HTTP with pipelining.
CS

questions.subtopic: Application layer protocols: DNS, SMTP, HTTP, FTP, Email
questions.explaination: Resolving the URL via 3-tier iterative DNS requires $3\text{ RTT}$. Initiating TCP connection and requesting the base HTML page requires $1 + 1 = 2\text{ RTT}$, so the base HTML is received after $3 + 2 = 5\text{ RTT}$. With persistent HTTP pipelining, all 10 objects are fetched in 1 round trip over the established connection, giving $5 + 1 = 6\text{ RTT}$ (D is TRUE). With non-persistent HTTP and 5 parallel connections, fetching 10 objects takes 2 sequential batches; each batch takes $1\text{ RTT (TCP)} + 1\text{ RTT (HTTP)} = 2\text{ RTT}$, adding $2 \times 2 = 4\text{ RTT}$, giving $5 + 4 = 9\text{ RTT}$ (C is TRUE).
